packets.description: United Natural Foods Q4 FY2026: verified profit and cash bridges, FY2027 investment demands, three valuation routes, nine-quarter history and dated signposts.

what_changed.summary: United Natural Foods Q4 FY2026: verified profit and cash bridges, FY2027 investment demands, three valuation routes, nine-quarter history and dated signposts.

items.title: Profit and next-year cash point in different directions.
items.detail: The EBITDA guide rises; the FCF midpoint falls. Capital plus cloud investment rises from $252M to about $300M. The company does not provide a full forward cash bridge, so the spending increase is context, not an exact explanation of every dollar.

items.title: The operating improvement survives the cyber adjustment.
items.detail: Q4 adjusted EBITDA removes a $3M net cyber benefit this year and adds back $26M of costs last year. The full-year subtraction is $21M. Keep those periods separate.

items.title: Sales contraction is not a measured organic decline.
items.detail: Management quantifies about 500 basis points of optimization headwind and 150 points of project unwind, with a favorable but unquantified cyber comparison. Those components do not establish underlying volume growth.

items.title: Cash is improving, with qualifications.
items.detail: Annual operating cash increased, but receivables and inventory released cash, stock compensation was added back, and receivable monetization has an economic cost. None of that makes cash unreal; it changes what can repeat.

items.title: Valuation is an assumption set, not a target borrowed from the Street.
items.detail: Our $49 uses disclosed guidance, observed debt and an explicit diluted-share assumption. A conditional entry near $39.20 provides a 20% discount to that value; the current price does not.

packets.title: Academy Sports (ASO): the tariff cash boost behind the earnings jump
packets.page_title: ASO Q2 FY2026 Research Packet - Charged Alpha
packets.description: ASO Q2 FY2026: verified profit and share-count bridges, tariff refund accounting, cash conversion, three valuation routes and dated signposts.

what_changed.summary: ASO Q2 FY2026: verified profit and share-count bridges, tariff refund accounting, cash conversion, three valuation routes and dated signposts.

items.title: Growth is real, but uneven.
items.detail: Total sales increased 3.0% while comps slipped 0.4%. The store base reached 327 and online sales grew 12.8%. Subtracting comp from total growth is not an exact new-store revenue bridge because the populations and denominators differ.

items.title: Profit did more of the EPS work than the share count.
items.detail: Net income grew 9.94%; diluted shares fell 6.11%. On an old-share-count-first bridge, higher profit adds about $0.18 per share and the lower denominator adds about $0.13. Neither effect should be mistaken for the other.

items.title: The tariff benefit is not a non-GAAP add-back.
items.detail: The $0.06 net EPS benefit remains in reported and adjusted performance. The actual adjusted-income bridge adds equity compensation and a debt-retirement loss, then deducts their tax effects.

items.title: Cash needs a wider lens.
items.detail: H1 operating cash includes tariff refunds, while $72.2M of tariff-claim remittances sits in financing. Reported adjusted FCF is $237.6M; subtracting that financing outflow gives a $165.3M cash illustration, not a measure of recurring FCF.

items.title: The rerating has used much of the valuation cushion.
items.detail: At our approximately $49.99 snapshot, the $50 central value offers almost no upside. The $33/$53/$68 scenarios have a $50 weighted value. A profitable retailer can still be an unattractive fresh purchase when uncertainty is high and the cushion is thin.

packets.title: Baozun (BZUN): the market prices its business at less than zero
packets.page_title: BZUN Q2 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Baozun (BZUN) Q2 2026 earnings research packet: the call, three valuation routes, scenarios, signposts, earnings quality, balance sheet, risks and catalysts — companion to the Charged Alpha episode.

what_changed.summary: Baozun (BZUN) Q2 2026 earnings research packet: the call, three valuation routes, scenarios, signposts, earnings quality, balance sheet, risks and catalysts — companion to the Charged Alpha episode.

items.title: The operating swing is real but seasonal.
items.detail: Q2 is a mid-size quarter; Q4 (Singles' Day) carries the year. Non-GAAP operating income of RMB74M in Q2 compares with RMB198M in Q4 2025 and RMB8M in Q1 2026 — read the trailing four quarters (RMB269M), not one print.

items.title: Group profit is not shareholder profit.
items.detail: Of RMB43.8M of Q2 net income, RMB26.8M went to minority holders — mostly Cainiao's 37% of the Baotong logistics arm — leaving RMB17.0M for Baozun's shareholders. Any valuation of 'the operating business' has to net this out.

items.title: The cash is the thesis, and it is real:
items.detail: RMB2.81B of cash and short-term investments against RMB1.24B of short-term loans — $231M net, $3.98 per ADS — but it sits inside a Cayman holding structure with minority holders owning 34% of total equity, a small VIE (4.4% of revenue) and a China-ADR discount that has persisted for years.

items.title: Management raised the bar on itself:
items.detail: the 2028 non-GAAP operating income target went from RMB550M (set March 2026) to at least RMB700M (August 2026). Consensus (3–6 analysts) sits at RMB586M for 2028 — the Street does not yet believe it.

items.title: The consumer is the risk, in their own words:
items.detail: E-Commerce product sales fell 9.6% on Home & Furnishing and Cosmetics, and the release says 'soft consumer sentiment'. If that spreads into the services line (63% of revenue), the margin story stalls.
